newsitem.title: USA: Newmont raises bid for Santa Fe Pacific to $2.2 billion.
newsitem.headline: Newmont raises bid for Santa Fe Pacific to $2.2 billion.

text.p: Newmont Mining Corp. said Tuesday it raised its unsolicited takeover bid for Santa Fe Pacific Gold in a stock offer worth $2.2 billion in its attempt to derail the company's proposed merger with Homestake Mining Co.

Santa Fe agreed in early December to be acquired by Homestake in a stock deal then valued at $17.42 per share, or $2.3 billion. But Homestake's bid of 1.115 of its shares for each Santa Fe share is now worth only $15.0525 per share, or $2.0 billion. Homestake's stock rose 37.5 cents to $13.50 at midday on the New York Stock Exchange.
Newmont is offering 0.40 share of its stock, worth $16.50, for each of Santa Fe's 133 million shares outstanding, far more than its initial offer of 0.33 of a share made on Dec. 5.
Newmont's stock edged down 12.5 cents to $41.375, while Santa Fe gained $1 to $15.25, both on the NYSE.
Newmont also said it has requested that Santa Fe enter into negotiations with it in order to terminate Santa Fe's merger agreement with Homestake.
In addition, Newmont said it is filing preliminary proxy materials with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday, and will begin its tender offer when it receives regulatory approval.

The offer is subject to the exchange of at least 90 percent of Santa Fe's common shares, the ability to merge with Santa Fe on a pooling of interests basis, and the withdrawal of Santa Fe's takeover defence plan.

"The combination of our two companies is the best fit at the best price with unparalleled opportunities to create long-term value," said Ronald C. Cambre, chairman, president and chief executive of Newmont.

"Santa Fe's principal assets are two large mines in Nevada, and its extensive and largely unexplored property position in the state. Our combination would bring to Santa Fe the advantages of Newmont's global exploration capability and operating cost-efficiency.

"Our two companies would benefit both from the proximity of each company's Nevada properties and from their complementary proprietary technologies. These are synergies that Santa Fe cannot achieve either on its own or in combination with any other company," Cambre said.

Newmont said that at the current gold price the merger would boost reserves immediately, increase earnings per share in the year after the deal closes and raise production and cash flow per share in the second year following closing.
Newmont Mining's sole asset is its 91 percent ownership of Newmont Gold Co., a leading global gold producer with operations in Nevada, Peru, Uzbekistan and Indonesia.
